outcome: Fresh source-bound native playtest proved active camp-guard precedence after a transient free-text follow intent: actors 18/19/20 were materialized with initial mission values 6/7/8, each accepted the exact native request and produced a native reply/begins-following chain, then all restored GUARD_ALLY with guard posts and held those posts while the player moved six squares west.
summary: The fixture supplied three independently named nearby allied actors: R031 Guard Ally 1 (character:18, initial GUARD_ALLY/mission 6), R031 Guard 1 (character:19, initial GUARD/mission 7), and R031 Patrol 1 (character:20, initial GUARD_PATROL/mission 8). Native inspections bound those identities before interaction (J0029, J0021, J0025). One exact utterance, follow me, was submitted through the native prompt and accepted (J0048). The run-bound native message/application chain records replies and begins-following transitions for all three (J0057, J0060, J0071), with runner requests req_0/req_1/req_2 and corroborating responses in config/llm_intent_runner.log. After ordinary applying turns, actor-bound native inspections show all three normalized to GUARD_ALLY with guard_post values (J0138, J0134, J0130). A native guarded move reached [3368,995,0] from [3374,995,0] (J0160); the final observation retains the actors at their guard-post positions (J0158). This proves precedence of active camp-guard ownership after transient follow intent. It does not separately prove durable mission-7 versus mission-8 semantics once both normalize to GUARD_ALLY, and it does not prove save/reload persistence.
